primary_source.title: Could Inference-Time Interventions Preserve Alignment? Safety Cost of Steering Vectors Is Separable and Reducible
primary_source.source_scope: Section 6.5, Table 5: constraint ablation on Llama-8B Corrigible at steering multiplier alpha=1.

assessment.core_failure_mode: Optimizing the safety/ASR objective without explicit effect-preservation and false-refusal constraints can yield numerically lower ASR while destroying the intended intervention effect and/or causing extreme benign over-refusal.
assessment.source_interpretation: The paper explicitly describes the no-both condition as the lowest ASR but catastrophic false refusals, nearly indiscriminate refusal, and the lowest behavioral score because most queries are refused.

scope_corrections: All deltas are relative to the unsteered baseline, not absolute ASR/effect/FRR levels.

This is a single constrained-optimization ablation on Llama-8B Corrigibility at alpha=1. It does not establish the same numeric tradeoff for other models, steering behaviors, post-training methods, or arbitrary activation interventions.
The evidence supports joint acceptance criteria for this intervention family; it does not prove that the paper's exact constraints are uniquely optimal or sufficient for all utility dimensions.
recommended_downstream_wording: For the reported Llama-8B Corrigibility steering ablation, ASR alone selects pathological solutions: removing both utility constraints slightly improves delta-ASR to -0.70 but drives delta-FRR to +50.43 and delta-effect to -4.15. Treat safety, benign refusal, and intended-effect preservation as joint acceptance axes, with this exact quantitative tradeoff limited to the tested setting.
